sources.entry: TomatoBar - World's neatest Pomodoro timer for macOS menu bar. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/ivoronin/TomatoBar) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
TomatoBar - Pomodoro Technique Timer for macOS with Touch Bar support.

summary.one_liner: TomatoBar is a Pomodoro timer that lives in the macOS menu bar, with configurable work and rest intervals, optional sounds, actionable notifications, and a global hotkey.
summary.what_it_does: TomatoBar runs as a Pomodoro technique timer in the macOS menu bar. It offers configurable work and rest intervals, optional timer sounds, discreet actionable notifications, and a global hotkey. It logs state transitions in JSON format to a log file in the app's cache directory, which the README suggests using for productivity analysis. It can also be controlled with tomatobar:// URLs, so the timer can be started or stopped from the command line with "open tomatobar://startStop". The README states the app is fully sandboxed with no entitlements. Touch Bar integration and macOS versions earlier than Big Sur are supported only by versions prior to 3.0.
use_cases: Run Pomodoro work and break intervals from the menu bar
Track focus sessions for studying or work
Start or stop a timer from the command line or scripts
Analyze productivity from a JSON event log
stack: Swift (macOS app, inferred; not named in README)
notable: Sandboxed macOS app with no entitlements, per the README
JSON state-transition log for external analysis
Touch Bar support in versions before 3.0
caveats: If the app does not start after a Homebrew install, the README suggests reinstalling with --no-quarantine
Touch Bar and pre-Big Sur macOS support only in versions before 3.0
Timer sounds are licensed from buddhabeats (licensing note in README)
